newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra keeps foreign limit on airport bids.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra keeps foreign limit on airport bids.

text.p: Australia said on Friday it would not cut foreign ownership limits for consortiums bidding for major government airports, but would allow a 180 day period of grace to reduce any foreign holdings to below the limit.

"The government takes seriously the foreign ownership limits ... and reaffirms its commitment to ensuring majority Australian ownership of airports," Finance Minister John Fahey and Transport Minister John Sharp said in a joint statement.
The government has set a 49 percent foreign ownership limit on bidders for major capital city and regional airports it is privatising through long-term leases.
Fahey and Sharp said the government had received several requests for an exemption to the limit.
"All firms bidding for the airport leases were aware of the legislated restrictions on foreign ownership," they said.
The government is finalising the privatisation of three main airports, Brisbane, Melbourne and Perth, and would announce the successful consortiums by the end of June, the ministers said.
Exemptions have already been made to allow foreign managed investment funds to participate if at least 60 percent of their money comes from Australians.
But the ministers said the government had decided to allow airport bidders which inadvertently breached the 49 percent foreign limit a 180-day grace to reduce the foreign holding.

Fahey announced earlier this month that the government had shortlisted 13 bids from six consortiums for the first stage of its sale of government airports around the country but did not name any of the successful or rejected consortiums.

The shortlisted bidders would present revised bids by mid-April after talks with the government team overseeing the sale and due diligence studies, Fahey said. The airports would be sold in a yet-to-be determined sequence.

The Australian Financial Review said in a report on Friday the future of a consortium headed by Lend Lease Corp and Brambles Ltd in the airport privatisation appeared uncertain after the government's ruling on foreign ownership.

Australian Airport Services, which had won a place on the short list for Brisbane, Melbourne and Perth airports, had sought an exemption to the ownership regulations which had been inadvertently breached by the passive foreign shareholdings in Brambles and Lend Lease, the newspaper said.

Offshore investors accounted for about 40 percent each of Brambles and Lend Lease. With Irish airport operator Aer Rianta taking up 20 percent of the AAS consortium, the total foreign shareholding would have exceeded the 49 per cent limit.
